    Troubleshooting

    Start with the first Console error. A Navigation Graph that fails to import cannot update its compiled runtime asset, so later runtime symptoms may be consequences of that authoring error.

    Package compilation

    ZLinq.dll or the ZLinq namespace is missing

    ZLinq.Unity is an adapter and does not contain the core library. Install the ZLinq NuGet package with NuGetForUnity first, then install the ZLinq.Unity UPM package. See Installation.

    If both are installed, verify that their versions are compatible and that the NuGet package produced the core assembly under Assets/Packages.

    LitMotion types are missing

    Install LitMotion 2.0.0 or newer with the Git URL in Installation. Allow Unity to finish importing LitMotion before installing or reimporting UITK Navigation.

    Graph authoring

    The Navigation Graph creation or editor menu is missing

    1. Verify that the project uses Unity 6000.6.0b5 or newer.
    2. Confirm that com.unity.graphtoolkit 0.5.0-exp.1 is resolved in Package Manager.
    3. Resolve the earliest Graph Toolkit or UITK Navigation compile error in the Console.
    4. Reimport the .uinavgraph after compilation succeeds.

    UITK Navigation uses Graph Toolkit for authoring and compiles the graph to a runtime UINavigationAsset; a Graph Toolkit error therefore blocks graph import. See Requirements.

    The graph reports validation errors

    Check these structural rules:

    • The graph contains at least one Screen node and exactly one Start node.
    • Start connects to exactly one Screen Enter.
    • Every Screen has a non-empty, unique Node ID.
    • A UI, Random, Portal, or continuing Action output connects to the required single target.
    • UI outputs do not duplicate the same trigger and address on one node.
    • Random has at least one connected output, non-negative finite weights, and a connected weight sum greater than zero.
    • Each Portal has a valid address, a unique condition, and exactly one target.
    • Time Scale and Scene Action values satisfy the constraints described by their node pages.

    Warnings for unregistered addresses do not always stop compilation, but they usually indicate that UXML and graph values no longer agree.

    Navigation at runtime

    Play Mode starts with a blank UI

    1. Make sure exactly one enabled UINavigatorBehaviour exists. A duplicate disables itself and logs an error.
    2. Assign the intended .uinavgraph to its Navigation Graph field.
    3. Verify that Start reaches the expected first UI node.
    4. Add the first View address to that UI node's On Enter > Show list.
    5. Confirm that a matching NavElement is attached to a live Player-context panel.
    6. Compare Category and Key exactly, including case.

    UINavigatorBehaviour waits briefly for Views to register, then initializes the graph. A View that never attaches to a panel cannot receive the initial Show command.

    A button, toggle, or signal does not navigate

    Match the sender, catalog tab, and graph trigger:

    Sender Catalog tab Graph route
    NavButton Button UI Button output or Button Portal
    NavToggle Button Toggle output or Toggle Portal with the expected On/Off value
    UINavigationEvents.RequestSignal(...) Signal Signal output or Signal Portal

    Then verify the exact Category / Key. Normal UI outputs are evaluated only on the active UI node; Portals are global and are tested before the active node. Scan Project can register a missing catalog entry, but it cannot correct a mismatched address or trigger type.

    More than one View animates at once

    This is expected when multiple attached NavElement instances share the same View address. The registry broadcasts Show and Hide commands to every matching instance. Give each independently controlled View a unique Category / Key.

    A UI View route occurs earlier than expected

    UI View outputs fire when a matching Animated Show or Hide transition starts, not when its animation completes. Instant View commands and InstantShow() or InstantHide() do not fire this output. Use a Time Delay, a different application signal, or another graph step when routing must wait.

    Transitions

    A View changes visibility but does not move

    • Confirm that the Move channel is enabled or that a preset containing Move was applied.
    • Ensure the animated element receives a non-zero resolved width and height from layout.
    • If the View starts with display: none, UITK Navigation performs a layout warm-up for up to four frames before starting a Move animation.
    • In UI Builder, selecting a preset applies its values to the Show/Hide channels and then resets the preset selector to None. Inspect the channel values rather than expecting the selector to remain selected.

    See Transition animation for channel precedence, timing, and Hide Mode.

    A transition, popup result, or async operation never completes

    Check every active animation channel for Loops = -1. Infinite channels repeat in Ping Pong mode and never report completion, so a visibility transition or Popup close that awaits them cannot settle. Use a finite loop count for lifecycle transitions.

    Animations continue while Time.timeScale is zero

    This is intentional by default. Navigation delays use unscaled time and transition animation starts with a real-time scheduler, so menus and Popups continue to work while gameplay is paused unless you replace the View scheduler.

    Back navigation

    Escape or the mouse Back button does nothing

    Add and enable UIBackInputRouter. It translates Escape, Backspace, and mouse Back/Forward buttons into navigation requests through the Input System.

    For graph history to handle Back, the active Screen must enable Use Back and history must contain a previous Screen. A visible View with Hide On Back or Block Back has priority. The topmost Popup has still higher priority: Close closes it, Block consumes Back, and PassThrough lets navigation below it continue.

    Popups

    UIPopupHost says the UI root is not ready

    Place UIPopupHost on the same GameObject as PanelRenderer, enable the renderer, and call Show only after the panel root has initialized. See Popups.

    A popup template is rejected

    The template must contain exactly one UIPopupView, exactly one UIPopupContent inside it, and zero or one UIPopupBackdrop. Remove duplicate wrappers and do not place the required Content outside the View.

    Clicking an action does not complete ShowAsync

    UIPopupActionButton with close-popup="false" raises its action but deliberately keeps the Popup open. Close its handle, call CloseTop, or set close-popup="true" when that action should complete the task.

    Scene Action nodes

    A scene does not load, activate, or unload

    • Add named or indexed scenes to Build Settings and verify the selected reference mode.
    • Set Active Loaded Scene and Unload Scene require the scene to be loaded already.
    • The last loaded scene cannot be unloaded.
    • If Allow Scene Activation is disabled on Load Scene, call UINavigatorBehaviour.ActivatePendingScene() when activation should continue.

    An Action node's Next chain continues immediately after the request is issued; it does not wait for Unity's asynchronous scene operation to finish. Trigger post-load UI from the destination scene or an explicit completion signal when ordering matters.

    The Key picker does not show an address

    Open Key Catalog, select the correct View/Button/Signal tab, and run Scan Project. Add code-only addresses manually because project scanning covers UXML and .uinavgraph assets, not arbitrary C# strings.
